### Architect · Answer

Event: `7073022206e09a773de6e1cbd19dca65` · 2026-09-29T04:37:45Z

> SSH1 facts and draft: .wash/local/SSH1-design.md (sunset 0.6.0 read and built in /tmp; nothing fetched into the tree).
> 
> 1. Signer: NO as published. The server signs H with an in-memory SignKey; a public-only host key panics. KEXINIT is hashed on arrival and rekeys are encrypted, so the fix is inside sunset: a patch mirroring its client AgentSign, a server event handing out keyd's exact sign_ssh_exchange fields (~150-250 lines). keyd signing an sshd-supplied hash needs the same event, saves only a KEXINIT copy, and loses R44's own-digest rule and 6 tests. Recommend: patch. A 2nd patch (~60-100 lines) is needed regardless: the server drops window-change, signal and break, which sshd.md requires.
> 2. Licence: 0BSD; deps MIT/Apache/BSD-3. sunset forbids unsafe and builds no_std for rv32 and rv64 (checked). Cost: 35 runtime crates (4 already vendored), incl. curve25519-dalek, a 2nd Ed25519 (sshd only; keyd unaffected), getrandom 0.4. Their unsafe is mostly SIMD that RISC-V never compiles; Miri runs on soft paths through force-soft cfgs. Feasible, several times smoltcp's set.
> 3. Sans-IO: yes (input/output/progress events). The trait is thin.
> 
> Draft: no_std core in servers/sshd + tools/sshd-host (stdin/stdout, keyd's own code in process so OpenSSH verifies keyd's hash end to end, a fixed login table, a scripted console). New Login rule: the query is answered by holds only; the steward is asked only after a verified signature. Loopback cases move to our server, plus R67 refusal cases; ONE OpenSSH reference case stays (server="openssh", SELinux probe). Node SSH1: Tier A, L, needs nothing unfinished.
> 
> Owner choice (sec. 3): a patched crate breaks vendor's "exactly as published". Recommend: published bytes + vendor/patches/sunset.patch checked by vendor-check; offer the patch upstream (needs the owner's word). Alternatives: wait for upstream; take sunset in-tree. Also: vendor in SSH1; curve25519-sha256 only, PQ kex on Open. I can file the decision_request.

The cost: it needs a patch so keyd signs the exchange (the host key never enters sshd; about 150-250 lines, mirroring sunset's own client agent signing), a second small patch for window-change, signal and break (60-100 lines, needed anyway), and 35 vendored crates (4 already vendored), including a second Ed25519 used only by sshd. >    - No: Keep OpenSSH's sshd for the loopback cases and fix the host instead

>    - Published bytes + checked patch file (recommended): vendor/sunset stays as published; vendor/patches/sunset.patch is applied at build and checked by vendor-check

>    - Take sunset in-tree: Our own copy, no longer 'vendored'; we own its maintenance
> 3. May we offer the signer and channel-request patches to sunset's author (a public PR or email under your name)?

>    - Not now: Carry the patch privately
> 4. Keep one reference case that runs OpenSSH's own sshd, so a bug shared by the bench's session driver and our server can't hide? It still hits SELinux under Wash, so it would run under --allow-skip or from your login session.
>    - Keep one reference case (recommended): server = "openssh", with the SELinux probe
>    - Drop it: Our server only; the client stays OpenSSH
> 5. Meanwhile, the six loopback cases fail under Wash's service context. Fix the host now?

>    - Local policy module: You install the one-rule module (unconfined_service_t -> unconfined_t transition)
>    - Run Wash as a user service: Agents get your login context; no policy change
> 6. Key exchange: curve25519-sha256 only, with post-quantum (sntrup/mlkem hybrid) left on sshd.md's Open list?
>    - curve25519 only, PQ on Open (recommended): Smallest; OpenSSH clients still connect
>    - Include a PQ hybrid now: More vendored code and review

Then write the design on sshd.md, testbench.md and vendor/README.md (planned sections, the Login rule, the reference case, the patch-file rule), add the SSH1 node (parent M1, Tier A, L, no unfinished needs) and commit the pages on redoubt with the owner's sign-off (git commit -s), staged by path. ### Architect · Answer

Event: `dc43e21f70a82104b9726a4c0ca0909e` · 2026-09-29T04:54:12Z

> Committed 1b5a9a34e on redoubt, signed off, 4 paths: sshd.md (planned "The core and its platforms", the Login rule, Open: box-call blocking + PQ), testbench.md (planned "Against Redoubt's sshd" with the reference case; planned "Patched crates"), vendor/README.md, todo/ssh-loopback-host.md. doccheck 0; vendor-check tests pass. Node SSH1 added (M1, package, no needs; Tier A, L in body); the sshd step now needs SSH1 too.
> 
> Ed25519: keyd and the loader use ed25519-compact 2.4.2 (no deps). It also does X25519, so sshd's Ed25519 verification AND its X25519 can both go through it. Options: (a) a verifier hook only saves ~2.6K lines, since curve25519-dalek stays for X25519; (b) keyd and the loader moving to dalek puts 30K lines into verified boot, rejected; (c) ed25519-compact as the shared crate removes curve25519-dalek, x25519-dalek, ed25519-dalek, ed25519 and signature, 30.2K vendored code lines, for ~80-150 more patch lines (sunset uses dalek at 20 sites: sign.rs, and 4 in kex.rs). Recommend (c); it's written in the pages as the design. The owner may overrule before start. This third change stays ours; only the signer and channel patches go upstream.
> 
> Flags:
> 1. Patch mechanism: vendor/sunset holds the published crate WITH the patch applied, because Cargo can't apply patches and a generated path breaks a plain build. SHA256SUMS records the published bytes, and vendor-check reverses the patch to check them. The decision option's text said "stays as published, applied at build". Same guarantee, different mechanics; tell me if the owner wants it the other way.
> 2. Finding: ed25519-compact (loader, keyd) is not vendored, against tenet 5. SSH1 vendors it (noted in the README).
> 
> Reading list, owned paths and traps: .wash/local/SSH1-implementer.md.
